requires: the target is an explicitly identified GitHub repository
the user explicitly requests a plugin test or audit
the GitHub app can read the target repository and write the harness request file
do_not_use_for: ordinary repository inspection or advisory review
a standalone ZIP, pasted code, or local folder without a GitHub repository target
a private target while this harness repository is public

request.request_id_rule: Generate a unique value for every requested run; never reuse the previous request_id.

execution: Resolve and verify the target repository, ref and plugin path before writing.
Read the current .audit/request.json and retain its blob SHA for an atomic update.
Write the complete request to .audit/request.json on main using the current blob SHA.
Read back the request and commit SHA; only that request-file change is the automatic ChatGPT trigger.
Locate the Full WordPress Plugin Audit run whose head SHA equals the request commit SHA.
Inspect job outcomes and the wordpress-plugin-audit artifact before interpreting findings.
Treat scanner failures as candidate findings; wordpressqualityarchitect confirms or rejects bugs against the applicable oracle.
Do not describe a green source/controlled-runtime audit as staging, production, browser/device or provider proof.
